Se pasa de una forma a la otra con dos t: You go from one form to the other with two theorems of vector calculus. The divergence theorem, $∮ A·dS = ∫ ∇·A dV$, turns the fluxes through closed surfaces (the two Gauss laws) into divergences. Stokes' theorem, $∮ A·dl = ∫ (∇ × A)·dS$, turns the circulations (Faraday and Ampère–Maxwell) into curls. That is why the two forms are equivalent; the differential one describes each point and the integral one is convenient when there is symmetry.
